author: Ninpro
quote:
When I genuinely struggle to think of things I dislike about a game, I know I've found something truly special. I played the original OoT only a couple of years ago for the first time, and persistently had the thought, "I wish I could experience this game the way it was meant to be experienced 30 years ago, before 3D games were polished enough to make it feel clunky by comparison."

I'm happy to say that this version of OoT is exactly what I had hoped for, and I've finally been able to see and feel the magic that so many felt when it first came out. The controls have been modernized to a mix between BotW and WW, the game looks better than any other Nintendo game, runs at a solid 60fps, the gameplay is fun, the dungeons are interesting, the already amazing story has been enhanced with cinematic moments, and the pacing is perfect: I never found myself getting bored with the gameplay.

If there's anything I could try to dock points for, it would be that the English voice acting isn't always great, and Zelda's face was a bit jarring the first time I saw it. So if you subtracted 0.2 for each of those things, that would technically make my score a 9.8/10.

Congrats to the younger Nintendo devs who were able to recapture 30 years later what made the original a timeless classic.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Ninpro
quote: +3 Points for the insane level of realism and world simulation. +1 point for being a video game that's actually fun to play. How in the world does Rockstar think it's acceptable to spend 13 years working on a game and instead deliver a relationship simulator at (hopefully) 30fps with a $100 price tag? There's no need to mention the rest of the problems and bugs with the game. You've already seen and heard them all by the time you've read this review. This game is the definition of everything wrong with AAA.
